sec.title: Background
sec.p: Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting immune checkpoint molecules such as programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1), which is expressed in both immune and tumour cells, are conventional immunotherapy approaches. Although approved as monotherapy for the first-line treatment of several cancers, mAbs targeting PD-L1 have shown limited efficacy in colorectal cancer (CRC). Here, we investigated if nucleic acids translated into anti-PD-L1 nanobodies (PDL1Nbs) effectively suppress CRC tumourigenesis in mouse models.

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: Mice were transplanted with MC-38 mouse sporadic CRC (sCRC) cells or challenged with azoxymethane and dextran sodium sulfate, a combination treatment that induces colitis-associated CRC (CAC). The tumour-bearing mice were treated with a PDL1Nb-encoding plasmid DNA (pDNA) delivered via polymers, or treated with PDL1Nb-encoding nucleoside-modified messenger RNA (PDL1Nb mRNA) delivered via lipid nanoparticles (LNP). Moreover, bone marrow haematopoietic stem cells (BMHSCs) were differentiated and maturated by treating growth factors in the presence of PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP or control luciferase mRNA-LNP with/without lipopolysaccharide. We examined sCRC tumour proliferation and growth, CAC tumour incidences and numbers, tumour infiltration of immune cells and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs).

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Polymer delivery of PDL1Nb pDNA efficiently repressed sCRC progression in tumour-bearing mice. Intriguingly, LNP delivery of the quadruple PDL1Nb (qPDL1Nb) mRNA showed a greater efficacy than the delivery of the monomeric PDL1Nb (mPDL1Nb) mRNA in suppressing sCRC tumour progression. Moreover, qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment significantly reduced CAC incidence. Mechanistically, PD-L1 blockade by qPDL1Nb resulted in marked decreases in tumour-infiltrating myeloid-derived suppressor cells and tumour-associated macrophages, as well as expression of PD-L1, but increases in tumour-infiltrating CD3+CD8+ cells during CAC tumourigenesis. Notably, in vitro LNP delivery of PDL1Nb mRNA into BMHSCs significantly inhibited their differentiation and maturation into BMDMs and strikingly reduced the expression of PD-L1, CD80, CD86 and CD206 in BMDMs.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: These results suggest that the PDL1Nb therapy is effective for both CAC and sCRC and using qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP is a promising alternative strategy for CRC immunotherapy.
Keywords: colorectal neoplasms, colitis, Crohn's disease, inflammatory bowel diseases

sec.title: WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN ON THIS TOPIC

list-item.p: The majority of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) with abundant myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) in the tumour immune microenvironment poorly respond to checkpoint inhibitors such as anti-cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 monoclonal antibody (CTLA-4 mAb), programmed cell death protein 1 mAb (PD-1 mAb) and programmed death-ligand 1 mAb (PD-L1 mAb).
PD-L1 mAb treatment does not significantly suppress azoxymethane/dextran sodium sulfate-induced colitis-associated CRC (CAC) tumourigenesis in wild-type (WT) mice.
mAbs have a large molecular size, a long half-life and a poor ability to penetrate tumours.
By contrast, nanobodies (Nbs) have a small size, a short half-life and a great ability to penetrate tumours.

Treatment with PDL1Nb-encoding plasmid DNA or nucleoside-modified messenger RNA (mRNA)-lipid nanoparticles (LNP) effectively repressed sporadic CRC progression and CAC tumourigenesis in WT and GNAI1;3 double knockout mice.
The quadruple PDL1Nb (qPDL1Nb) translated from LNP-delivered mRNA had a longer half-life than monomeric PDL1Nb (mPDL1Nb) in vivo.
Treatment with the qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP showed a greater efficacy than mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP in immunotherapy.

qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment significantly reduced CAC incidence, proliferation and PD-L1 expression in tumour and immune cells. Such treatment also markedly diminished tumour infiltration of MDSCs and tumour-associated macrophages but increased tumour infiltration of CD8+ T cells.

PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment dramatically inhibited bone marrow haematopoietic stem cells to differentiate and maturate into bone marrow-derived macrophages and reduced their expression of PD-L1, CD80, CD86 and CD206.

sec.title: HOW THIS STUDY MIGHT AFFECT RESEARCH, PRACTICE OR POLICY

list-item.p: Nucleoside-modified mRNA-LNP vaccines have proven highly effective in protecting against COVID-19-associated severe disease and death.
It is expected that the mRNA-LNP platform technology will achieve great success in immunotherapy to treat CRC.
Our results support that immunotherapy with PD-1 mAbs, which block the interaction of PD-1 with PD-L1 is effective in treating a minority of patients with CRC.
Our findings suggest that the use of qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment might be a promising alternative approach for treating both minority and majority subsets of patients with CRC.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Colorectal cancer (CRC) encompasses both sporadic CRC (sCRC) and colitis-associated CRC (CAC) and is the third most common cancer in the USA.1 Although the incidence of CAC has decreased among people who are older than 55 years of age due to colonoscopy screening, it has markedly increased in people who are younger than 55 years of age.1 In the early stages, CRC usually shows no symptoms, and it is difficult to be identified if a colonoscopy procedure is not performed. Once it is diagnosed, the majority of patients with CRC are already at advanced stages, making CRC the second leading cause of cancer-associated deaths in the USA.1 Therefore, there is an urgent need for better therapeutic strategies for the disease.

The primary mechanism of cancer immunotherapy is to modulate and enhance innate and adaptive immune responses, thereby enabling the immune system to better recognise and eliminate malignant cells. Although various types of immunotherapy have been applied in clinical cancer treatment, the outcomes remained largely unsatisfactory until a series of groundbreaking clinical trial results emerged in 2012.2,4 These trials have marked a turning point by employing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting immune checkpoint molecules such as cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4), programmed death-1 (PD-1) and programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1).2,4 Among these checkpoints, PD-1 and PD-L1 are an important pair and belong to the same family of receptors as CTLA-4 and CD28.2,4 PD-L1 and PD-L2, the ligands of PD-1, are expressed both on the surface of antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and on tumour cells, enabling tumours to evade immune surveillance and thereby promoting tumour progression and metastasis.

CTLA-4 is expressed on regulatory T cells and activated CD4+ or CD8+ T cells.4 CTLA-4 and CD28 share the same ligands, B7-1 (CD80) and B7-2 (CD86), which are expressed on APCs. When CTLA-4 competes with CD28 for binding B7-1 and B7-2, the differentiation process of CD4+ T cells into T helper 1 cells will be blocked, and meanwhile, the production of interferon-gamma (IFNγ), tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNFα) and interleukin-2 (IL-2), all of which promote proliferation of CD8+ T cells, will be inhibited.4,6 Therefore, the CTLA-4, PD-1 and PD-L1 checkpoints are great targets for cancer immunotherapy. Interestingly, although the CTLA4, CD274 and PDCD1 gene expressions are higher in CRC tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes than those in healthy colonic lymphocytes,7 anti-CTLA-4 mAbs (CTLA-4 mAbs) failed to show a significant efficacy when administered as a single-agent therapeutic regimen in patients with refractory metastatic sCRC.8 By contrast, anti-PD-1 mAbs have proven exceedingly effective as single-agent therapy for metastatic sCRC with high microsatellite instability (MSI-H), and thereby have been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as the first-line treatment for advanced metastatic sCRC.9 However, the utility of these mAbs in CRC therapy has been hampered by their unsatisfactory efficacy and inadequate responses in most patients with CRC with low or sufficient MSI (MSI-L and MSS, respectively). Moreover, the availability of this utility has been restrained by various factors including their high cost, limited tumour tissue penetration rate, large molecular size, immunogenicity and the occurrence of severe immune-related adverse effects. To this end, the development of better immune checkpoint inhibitors and the usage of alternative, potentially less expensive delivery platforms are critical for treating patients with CRC.

A nanobody (Nb) is a unique single-domain variable heavy chain region antibody whose molecular weight is approximately 15 kDa.10,12 Nbs, which were originally discovered in camelids and sharks,10 are characterised by small size, high stability, solubility, high affinity and cavity binding capability, as well as strong tissue penetrability with low immunogenicity.10,12 Due to their small size, abundant Nbs can be quickly cleared by the kidneys through renal excretion. The current approach for Nb production involves the insertion of Nb genes into expression vectors and subsequent expression in bacterial, yeast or mammalian systems followed by affinity purification. To increase the half-life and slow down renal excretion of small molecules, an approach has been taken by fusing them with other factors such as albumin or the crystallisable fragment (Fc) domain of the IgG.10,12 KN035-Fc is the first anti-PD-L1 Nb (PDL1Nb) approved for treating melanoma and MSI-H solid tumours in China.13 14 Compared with PD-L1 mAb (durvalumab) at high doses (eg, 0.92 mg/kg), intraperitoneal injection of KN035-Fc at relatively low doses (eg, 0.5 mg/kg) greatly triggers IFNγ production and inhibits A375 melanoma cell progression.13 Subsequently, CTLA-4Nb purified from a bacterial expression system demonstrated considerable capacity to suppress the growth of breast cancer, hepatoma and melanoma in syngeneic mouse models.15 16 However, the drawback of Nbs purified from the bacterial and yeast systems is the potential toxin contamination, incorrect methylation and misfolding. Moreover, Nbs purified from the mammalian expression system may be relatively safer, but the output is insufficient. Furthermore, the quick clearance of Nbs by the kidneys may reduce the efficacy of the Nb therapy.

Plasmid DNA (pDNA) and in vitro-transcribed (IVT) mRNAs can be used to deliver genetic information into living cells. For example, lipid nanoparticles (LNP)-encapsulated IVT nucleoside-modified (N1-methylpseudouridine-containing) mRNA vaccines against COVID-19 have been an exciting and greatly successful avenue for mitigating the serious consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic.17 In this study, we present the remarkable effects of delivery of pDNAs and mRNA-LNP encoding PDL1Nbs on suppressing CRC tumourigenesis in a syngeneic sCRC mouse model and a CAC model.

sec.title: Mice
sec.p: Mice on the C57BL/6;129 or C57BL/6 background were housed in a specific pathogen-free vivarium at University of Hawaii according to the NIH guidelines. G protein alpha inhibitory 1 (GNAI1) and GNAI3 double knockout (KO) (GNAI1;3DKO) and their control wild-type (WT) mice on the C57BL/6;129 background were described in our previous studies.18 19

sec.title: Cell lines and culture
sec.p: The MC-38 mouse sCRC cell line was obtained from Kerafast, and the human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK293) cell line was purchased from the American Type Culture Collection. Cells were cultured in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium with 10% heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum (FBS).

sec.title: DNA plasmid construction, preparation and transfection
sec.p: CTLA-4Nb or PDL1Nb mouse complementary DNA (cDNA) linked with a serum albumin secretion signal (ASS) at the 5’ end and a FLAG tag at the 3’ end, or a firefly luciferase (Luc) cDNA was inserted into the piggyBac expression vector, followed by DNA sequencing confirmation and plasmid preparation.20 DNA plasmids were stably transfected into HEK293 cells via G418 selection.

sec.title: In vitro transcribed mRNA
sec.p: Codon-optimised coding sequences of Luc, or FLAG (C-terminus) and ASS (N-terminus) fused with monomeric (m) CTLA-4Nb, mPDL1Nb or quadruple (q) PDL1Nb (qPDL1Nb) containing four individual mPDL1Nbs, which were connected by a 9-amino acid Gly-Gly-Gly-Gly-Ser-Gly-Gly-Gly-Ser (GS) linker, were synthesised and cloned into a base/nucleotide-modified mRNA production plasmid as described.21 Nucleotide-modified mRNA production was performed as described, purified by a cellulose purification strategy, and encapsulated in LNPs (Acuitas Therapeutics).21

sec.title: Tumour growth and treatment
sec.p: MC-38 cells (1×106 in phosphate-buffered saline) were injected subcutaneously into C57BL/6 WT mice. The tumour-bearing mice were treated and tumour volumes were measured twice per week and calculated as length×width×height/2 or length×width2/2.

sec.title: Colitis-associated colorectal cancer
sec.p: CAC was induced by azoxymethane (AOM, Sigma-Aldrich)/dextran sulfate sodium (DSS, MW 36–50 kDa, MP Biomedicals) as described previously in our study.18 Mice were treated and sacrificed on day 63, followed by desired experiments.

sec.title: Isolation of lamina propria via CAC tumour cells
sec.p: The isolation of colonic lamina propria from CAC tumour cells (cLPT) was previously described in our study.18

sec.title: BMHSC isolation and BMDM differentiation and maturation
sec.p: Bone marrow (BM) cells, which contain bone marrow haematopoietic stem cells (BMHSCs), were isolated from femurs of C57BL/6 WT mice. The isolated cells were resuspended in RPMI1640 medium supplemented with 10% FBS, 1× antibiotic-antimycotic and 1× non-essential amino acids, pooled, mixed and evenly distributed into four culture dishes per treatment group, and then differentiated into BMHSC-derived macrophages (BMDMs) via 20 ng/mL granulocyte‑macrophage colony‑stimulating factor (GM-CSF), 20 ng/mL granulocyte colony‑stimulating factor (G-CSF) and 10 ng/mL interleukin-6 (IL-6).18 19 22 At the same time, cultures were treated with Luc mRNA-LNP or mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP (1 µg/mL) and incubated for 6 days. On day 6, the cultures were divided into two groups: one group was cultured for an additional day without further treatment; the other was collected for BMDM maturation. The cells were resuspended at 1×10⁶ cells/mL, seeded in 6-well plates (triplicate wells per condition) and cultured with the same condition in the presence of 100 ng/mL lipopolysaccharide (LPS) for 24 hours. The BMDMs were collected for flow cytometry analysis.

sec.title: Flow cytometry
sec.p: Flow cytometry analysis via fluorescence minus one (FMO) was described in our previous studies.1822,24

sec.title: Immunoblotting
sec.p: Immunoblotting (IB) analysis was described previously in our studies.1822,24

sec.title: Immunohistochemistry
sec.p: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was performed as described in our previous studies.18 24 25

sec.title: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
sec.p: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was described in our previous studies.1822,24

sec.title: Statistical analysis
sec.p: Data were expressed as mean±SD. Statistical analysis was conducted using a two-tailed Student’s t-test or one-way analysis of variance. Statistical analyses were performed in GraphPad Prism V.8.0 (GraphPad Software) and significant differences were defined as a p value <0.05.

sec.title: Polymer nanoparticle delivery of PDL1Nb pDNAs inhibits sCRC progression and CAC tumour incidence
sec.p: Introducing pDNAs encoding Nbs in vivo can circumvent the issues associated with Nb production and purification and replenish Nbs rapidly cleared by the kidneys due to their small size. Using a well-established piggyBac plasmid,20 26 we generated highly efficient expression vectors containing a FLAG-tagged mouse PDL1Nb or CTLA-4Nb gene linked with an albumin secretion sequence (ASS), or a firefly Luc gene (figure 1A). The PDL1Nb pDNA (PDL1Nb-P), CTLA-4Nb pDNA (CTLA-4Nb-P) or Luc-pDNA (Luc-P) was stably transfected into HEK293 cells, and secreted PDL1Nb or CTLA-4Nb in the serum-free medium (SFM) was confirmed by IB (figure 1B). A band with the expected molecular weight for either PDL1Nb or CTLA-4Nb was detected (figure 1B). Interestingly, an extra band with a larger molecular weight was observed in the PDL1Nb but not CTLA-4Nb samples in HEK293 cells (figure 1B, right panel), indicating that PDL1Nb is specifically post-translationally modified in HEK293 cells with an unknown mechanism. Then, we determined whether PDL1Nb-P or CTLA-4Nb-P delivered via polymer nanoparticle (PNP) has a comparable effect to PD-L1 mAb on suppressing mouse sCRC MC-38 tumour development in a syngeneic mouse model. The PNP delivery of PDL1Nb-P but not Luc-P significantly suppressed MC-38 mouse sCRC development (figure 1C, D). As expected, PD-L1 mAb treatment also significantly inhibited MC-38 tumour growth (figure 1D). In comparison, the PNP delivery of PDL1Nb-P had a similar effect to PD-L1 mAb treatment on suppressing MC-38 sCRC tumour development (figure 1D), indicating that PNP-PDL1Nb-P could be an alternative for treating sCRC. By contrast, the PNP delivery of CTLA-4Nb-P did not attenuate MC-38 tumour growth (figure 1D). Taken together, our data suggest that the PNP delivery of PDL1Nb-P significantly suppresses sCRC tumourigenesis.

sec.p: PD-L1 is upregulated during CRC tumourigenesis.27,29 Consistent with a previous report,30 PD-L1 mAb treatment did not significantly reduce CAC tumour incidences in an AOM-induced and DSS-induced CAC model (figure 2A, B), which mimics the molecular and pathogenic process of human CAC.18 However, the PNP delivery of PDL1Nb-P significantly diminished CAC tumour incidence (figure 2C). We previously reported that loss of both GNAI1 and GNAI3 (GNAI1;3) led to many more CAC tumour incidences than WT controls.18 PNP delivery of PDL1Nb-P markedly reduced CAC tumour numbers in the colon compared with Luc-P treatment (figure 2D). Altogether, these results suggest that the PNP delivery of PDL1Nb-P represses CAC tumourigenesis in a mouse model.

sec.title: Delivery of PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP suppresses sCRC tumourigenesis
sec.p: A concern associated with delivering pDNA into the host is the potential integration of DNA vector into the host genome triggering mutagenesis and subsequent oncogenesis (known as genotoxic effects).31 To avoid this adverse event, we employed an mRNA-LNP immunotherapy strategy, which is derived from the mRNA vaccine strategy that has been successfully used for preventing COVID-19.1732,34 Linearised DNA templates containing monomeric or quadruple repeats of PDL1Nb, mCTLA-4Nb or Luc were in vitro transcribed to nucleoside-modified mRNAs and formulated to LNP (figure 3A).32 35 Except Luc construct, in each construct, there was a FLAG-tag and an ASS sequence, which were added to PDL1Nb and CTLA-4Nb. In the template containing qPDL1Nb repeats, each repeat was connected by a 9-amino acid GS linker (figure 3A). To verify that the mRNA-LNP can be translated into protein, we incubated HEK293 cells with different amounts of mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP, qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP or control Luc mRNA-LNP and then determined the levels of mPDL1Nb and qPDL1Nb secreted from the cells by IB via an anti-FLAG mAb. The presence of mPDL1Nb in the SFM of HEK293 cell culture was initially detected at a minimal level after 10 hours and peaked at 48 hours following treatment (figure 3B). Likewise, incubation of HEK293 cells with qPDL1 mRNA-LNP or Luc mRNA-LNP led to production and secretion of qPDL1Nb but not Luc from HEK293 cells because the Luc mRNA-LNP does not have a FLAG and an ASS sequence (figure 3C). Like PDL1Nb-P (figure 1B), mPDL1Nb mRNA produced equal doublet bands (figure 3B). To verify whether mPDL1Nb mRNA also produces the equal doublet bands in vivo, mice were injected intramuscularly with mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP or Luc mRNA-LNP. IB analysis revealed only one band for mPDL1Nb at the expected size (figure 3D). Overall, PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP is efficiently translated in the cells.

sec.p: Next, we elucidated if delivery of mPDL1Nb or mCTLA-4Nb mRNA-LNP mitigates MC-38 sCRC tumour progression. Administration of mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP via intramuscular injection appeared to reduce MC-38 sCRC tumour growth compared with the Luc mRNA-LNP control, although this inhibition was not statistically significant (figure 3E). By contrast, treatment with mCTLA-4Nb mRNA-LNP had no apparent effect on MC-38 sCRC tumour growth compared with the Luc mRNA-LNP control (figure 3F). Intriguingly, combined treatment of mCTLA-4Nb mRNA-LNP with mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP even slightly reduced the inhibitory effect of mPDL1Nb on inhibiting MC-38 sCRC tumour progression (figure 3G). We then determined the levels of mPDL1Nb in the blood of mice in the model on days 7, 9, 10, 11, 18 and 40, with mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP injections on days 8, 11, 15, 18, 22 and 25. The mPDL1Nb peaked at about 100 mg/mL in 24 hours and dipped to approximately 30 mg/mL 3 days after injection (figure 3H). These results suggest that most of the mPDL1Nb might be quickly cleared, and mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP together with mCTLA-4Nb mRNA-LNP does not synergise to inhibit MC-38 tumour growth effectively.

Subsequently, we assessed if the quadruple repeat format enhances the activity of PDL1Nb improving the efficacy of anti-MC-38 sCRC therapy. The qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP and mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP, which produced PDL1Nb at the same micromoles, were injected intramuscularly into mice bearing MC-38 tumour on days 14, 16, 18, 20 and 22 after initial inoculation of MC-38 sCRC cells. The qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment significantly inhibited MC-38 tumour growth, and this inhibition commenced 20 days after inoculation of MC-38 sCRC cells and the third injection of qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP (figure 3I). Further serum analysis revealed a proximal twofold increase in qPDL1Nb compared with mPDL1Nb in the blood after the second injection (figure 3H and J). Therefore, these results suggest that qPDL1Nb is more slowly cleared by the kidneys and has better therapeutic efficacy than that of mPDL1Nb in repressing MC-38 sCRC tumour progression.

sec.title: qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment impedes CAC and stimulates antitumour immunity
sec.p: The observations above prompted us to evaluate further if the qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment significantly reduces CAC proliferation and tumourigenesis. Initially, we explored if this treatment suppresses CAC tumourigenesis in WT mice in an AOM/DSS-induced CAC mouse model (figure 4A).18 The qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment significantly reduced CAC tumour numbers in WT mice compared with the Luc mRNA-LNP treatment (figure 4B). Following this, we unravelled if the qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment diminished CAC tumourigenesis in GNAI1;3DKO mice. Similar to our previous report,18 GNAI1;3 loss exceedingly promoted CAC tumourigenesis compared with WT control (figure 4C). Importantly, qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment significantly reduced CAC tumour numbers in the colon compared with controls of GNAI1;3DKO mice (figure 4C). IHC analysis further revealed that qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP reduced CAC tumour proliferation, although the reduction did not reach statistical significance (figure 4D, E).

sec.p: It is known that PD-L1 blockade releases brakes on immune cells and tumour cells, thus allowing T cells to attack and eradicate tumour cells. To understand the mechanisms by which qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment impedes colorectal tumourigenesis, we initially assessed its impact on MDSCs, which are defined as CD11b+Gr-1+ cells including monocytic CD11b+Ly6C+ MDSCs (mMDSCs) and are critical for AOM/DSS-induced CAC tumourigenesis and immune suppression.18 36 37 cLPTs were isolated and subjected to flow cytometry analysis. Consistent with our previous study,18 CD11b+Gr-1+ and monocytic MDSCs were significantly accumulated in the CAC tumour immune microenvironment (TIME) of GNAI1;3DKO mice compared with WT controls (figure 4F, G). The accumulation of CD11b+Gr-1+ MDSCs in GNAI1;3DKO mice was significantly blocked (figure 4F), or of mMDSCs and Gr+ cells was reduced without statistical significance by the qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment (figure 4F, G; online supplemental figure S1). Interestingly, tumour-associated macrophages (TAMs) (CD11b+F/480+) were notably accumulated in the CAC TIME of GNAI1;3DKO mice compared with WT controls, and the qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment showed a tendency to reduce this accumulation (figure 4H).

Next, we investigated whether the qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment enhances T cell immunity. In contrast to the downregulation of MDSCs and TAMs, the qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment significantly increased tumour infiltration of CD8+ T cells (figure 5A) and showed a trend towards increased levels of CD8+IFNγ+, CD4+ and CD4+IFNγ+ T cells in GNAI1;3DKO mice (figure 5B; online supplemental figure S2A, B). Since PD-L1 is a key target of and its expression is primarily induced by IFNγ,38 we examined its levels in CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. As shown, the qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment notably increased the level of CD4+PD-L1+ and CD8+PD-L1+ T cells in GNAI1;3DKO mice (figure 5C; online supplemental figure S2C). On the other hand, the qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment significantly diminished PD-L1 expression in EpCAM+ tumour cells (figure 5D), and also modestly affects its expression in overall CD45+ immune cells including TAMs in GNAI1;3DKO mice (online supplemental figures S2D-F). Similarly, the qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment increased the levels of CD8+ and CD8+PD-L1+ T cells but reduced the levels of PD-L1 in CD45+ immune cells including TAMs and EpCAM+ tumour cells of WT mice, although the trends were not statistically significant (figure 5E, F; online supplemental figures S3A-C). Consistent with figure 4D, treatment with qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP showed a trend towards inhibiting tumour cell proliferation, as measured by the level of BrdU incorporation into DNA in tumour epithelial cells (figure 5G), although the results did not reach statistical significance. Taken together, our results demonstrate that qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment substantially inhibits CAC tumourigenesis, markedly reduces tumour-infiltrating MDSCs, TAMs and PD-L1 expression, while apparently enhancing tumour-infiltrating CD4+ and CD8+ T cells.

sec.title: mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP stifles macrophage differentiation, maturation and PD-L1 expression
sec.p: TAMs in the TIME are predominantly derived from circulating monocytes with BMHSC origin and play an important role in CD8+ T cell exhaustion and CRC tumourigenesis.39 40 To determine whether PDL1Nb mRNA delivery by LNP has a direct effect on macrophage differentiation and maturation, we carried out an in vitro BMHSC differentiation and maturation assay. Bone marrow cells containing BMHSCs isolated from WT mice were differentiated into bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) via growth factors including G-CSF, GM-CSF and IL-6 and then matured by LPS in the presence or absence of mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP or Luc mRNA-LNP. mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP, but not Luc mRNA-LNP, significantly inhibited differentiation of BMHSCs into BMDMs (figure 6A). Moreover, mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP markedly inhibited BMDM maturation during differentiation or LPS-induced BMDM maturation as indicated by the expression levels of APC maturation markers CD80 and CD86 (figure 6B, C). CD80 and CD86 are critical for T cell activation, but they are also expressed in TAMs leading to immunosuppression.41 CD206, which is expressed in TAMs, promotes CRC progression and is associated with a poor prognosis of CRC,42 was induced at a low level during BMDM differentiation (figure 6D). mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP greatly diminished CD206 expression in macrophages (figure 6D). Unlike CD80, CD86 and CD206, the level of CD68, which is also a marker of TAMs and whose high level is associated with favourable outcomes in CRC, particularly in colon cancer and MMR-proficient CRC,43 44 was only slightly affected by mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP (figure 6E).

sec.p: To understand how mPDL1Nb mRNA inhibited macrophage differentiation and LPS-induced maturation, we measured the levels of PD-L1 in differentiated and maturated BMDMs. A high PD-L1 level was detected on Luc mRNA-LNP treatment, and by contrast, an extremely low level of PD-L1 was detected on the cell surface of differentiated BMDMs in the presence of mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment (figure 6F). Similarly, the level of PD-L1 on the surface of LPS-induced matured BMDMs was notably reduced by the mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment compared with that of the Luc mRNA-LNP treatment (figure 6F). However, compared with differentiated BMDMs, LPS was still able to significantly stimulate PD-L1 expression when it induced BMDMs maturation in the presence of mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP (figure 6F).
Taken together, our data suggest that PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment inhibits the differentiation and maturation of macrophages and reduces their surface levels of PD-L1, CD80, CD86 and CD206.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: CTLA-4, PD-1 and PD-L1 checkpoint blockades have been widely used for treating many types of cancers.4 45 PD-1 mAb was approved in 2020 by the FDA as the first-line drug for treating metastatic CRC with MSI-H, which comprises about 15% of CRC and elicits an immune response resulting in a ‘hot’ CRC. However, about 85% of patients with CRC are MSI-L/MSS, which respond poorly to CTLA-4 mAbs, PD-1 mAbs or PD-L1 mAbs, and hence are referred to as ‘cold’ CRC. Therefore, developing new regimens and strategies for treating CRC is critical. Here, we report that the PNP delivery of PDL1Nb pDNA and the LNP delivery of PDL1Nb mRNA suppress sCRC and CAC tumourigenesis in preclinical models.

Monoclonal Abs possess properties of large molecular mass and immunogenicity, leading to limited tumour tissue penetration and potential immune-related adverse effects. Conversely, Nbs are single-domain antibodies characterised by small size, lower immunogenicity and high tissue penetrability.10 Thus, in comparison with mAbs, Nbs could offer a superior option for treating CRC. However, the utility of Nb is encumbered by quick renal clearance, potential contamination during production and misfolding if produced and purified from bacteria and yeast or low production yields if expressed and purified from mammalian systems. A strategy of fusing Nb with the Fc fragment of IgG that increases the size and slows down the renal clearance rate has been successfully used to generate a PDL1Nb-Fc (KN035-Fc), which is produced in and purified from mammalian cells and has been approved to treat MSI-H solid tumours.13 14 In this study, we employed an approach involving the in vivo production of Nbs, ensuring a continuous supply of Nbs throughout the treatment process.

We have demonstrated that the PNP delivery of PDL1Nb pDNA effectively reduced sCRC and CAC tumourigenesis. However, like many other gene therapies, the delivery of PDL1Nb pDNA into cells might have an impact on the host genome. Given that nucleoside-modified mRNA-LNP vaccines developed by Moderna and Pfizer against COVID-19 had proved to be successful,1732,34 mRNA-LNP was also used for mAb therapy in preclinical and clinical studies. We, therefore, leveraged the mRNA-LNP platform and determined if LNP delivery of PDL1Nb mRNA greatly repressed sCRC and CAC progression. Of note, the use of N1-methylpseudouridine in the mRNA is important to maximise protein production from the IVT mRNA as well as minimise its innate inflammatory capacity. We engineered monomeric and quadruple forms of PDL1Nb mRNA and discovered that via intramuscular injections the LNP delivery of qPDL1Nb mRNA significantly reduced sCRC tumour progression, whereas mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP diminished sCRC tumour growth but did not reach statistical significance. This discovery demonstrates that the qPDL1Nb construct poses a longer serum half-life for a 60 kDa qPDL1Nb compared with a 15 kDa mPDL1Nb and thus offers superior efficacy over mPDL1Nb in treating CRC. In this regard, qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP was further tested for its effect on CAC tumourigenesis. Delivery of qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP via intramuscular injection significantly reduced CAC tumours in the colon of WT and GNAI1;3DKO mice. Our finding demonstrates that PD-L1 inhibitors can be used to treat CAC and that PDL1Nb is superior to PD-L1 mAb, which fails to suppress AOM/DSS-induced CAC tumourigenesis in WT mice.30

Compared with CAC and hot sCRC, the majority of cold CRCs have low frequencies of tumour-infiltrating T lymphocytes and dendritic cells but abundant MDSCs and TAMs leading to a suppressive TIME and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors.45 MDSCs and TAMs are key immune suppressor cells and promote the development of CAC and sCRC.1836 45,47 In our therapeutic strategy of combining the LNP with qPDL1Nb mRNA for CRC therapy via an intramuscular route, LNP can trigger T cell and humoral responses,35 and LNP-delivered qPD-L1 mRNA can continuously be in vivo translated to PDL1Nb that targets PD-L1 and blocks its interaction with PD-1, thereby further stimulating T cell activity. Moreover, LNP-delivered qPDL1Nb mRNA exhibits strong antitumour immunity by markedly reducing tumour infiltration of MDSCs and TAMs but increasing tumour-infiltrating CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and their expression of IFNγ, which plays a crucial role in activating T cell immunity in the CAC TIME.48 Interestingly, on qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment, the PD-L1 levels on the surface of CD45+ immune cells including TAMs or EpCAM+ tumour cells were reduced, whereas its levels were enhanced on CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Since IFNγ is a primary factor in driving PD-L1 expression,38 49 it is reasonable to presume that PD-L1 expression is upregulated by CD4+ and CD8+ T cells during CAC tumourigenesis, and that this PD-L1 upregulation could be an alternative indication of T cell activation.

Besides, intramuscular injection of qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP might circulate in the bloodstream and enter BMHSCs or tumour tissues affecting TAM differentiation or maturation of tumour-infiltrating monocytes originated from BMHSC. Indeed, co-incubation of mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP with BMHSCs in vitro, where mPDL1Nb is produced, secreted and remained present in the medium over time, significantly inhibits both BMDM differentiation and maturation and LPS-induced macrophage maturation, as marked by elevated levels of CD80 and CD86. In the TIME, CD80+, CD86+ or CD206+ TAMs promote T cell immunosuppression and CRC progression, especially at the advanced stage.42 43 50 51 The mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment markedly reduced their expression in BMDMs. At the same time, the mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment only had a trivial impact on CD68 expression. Studies suggest that a high density of CD68+ TAMs in MMR-proficient CRC is associated with a favourable 5-year survival rate.44 52

In addition, the mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment dramatically reduced the levels of PD-L1 on the surface of BMDMs during differentiation or LPS-induced maturation. This phenotype could be attributed to the delivery of mPDL1Nb mRNA into BMDMs, where the mRNA is translated and then binds to cytoplasmic PD-L1, resulting in the prevention of its cell surface transportation. Alternatively, mPDL1Nb mRNA might interfere with the translation of endogenous PD-L1 mRNA. Nevertheless, our study suggests that either mPDL1Nb or qPDL1Nb can attenuate macrophage differentiation from BMHSCs or monocytes if their presence in the TIME is maintained at the therapeutic level, and that the PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP therapeutic strategy is well-suited for treating cold CRC.

However, CRC tumourigenesis is a consequence of multifaceted effects, and a single-agent therapy is unlikely to eliminate CRC tumours. Combined therapeutic strategies have greater efficacy in treating CRC. For instance, a clinical trial showed that a combination of PD-1 mAb with CTLA-4mAb enhanced survival duration of metastatic CRC patients.53 Intriguingly, in our preclinical mouse model, the combination of mPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP with mCTLA-4 mRNA-LNP did not achieve a synergistic effect in treating sCRC. The plausible reasons are that CTLA-4 expression occurs in the early stage while PD-L1 is expressed in the late stage of CRC development,45 and the kidneys might quickly clear mNbs. Moreover, although LNP delivery of qPDL1Nb mRNA offered better efficacy in treating CRC, this treatment only reduced but did not abolish CRC tumourigenesis. In this context, there is an unmet need for strategies combining different anti-immune-checkpoint Nbs in a single mRNA-LNP construct or combining qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP with chemotherapy, targeted therapy or radiotherapy for the treatment of CRC.

sec.title: Study limitations
sec.p: The present study has several limitations. First, only mouse CTLA-4Nb and PDL1Nb nuclear acid drugs were used in this study. Given that mouse CTLA-4 pDNAs or mRNA-LNP have no apparent effect on inhibiting CRC tumour growth in mouse CRC models, whereas human CTLA-4 mAbs have been approved for treating MSI-H CRC, it is critical to determine whether human CTLA-4Nb and PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP significantly suppress human CRC tumourigenesis. Second, only CRC tumourigenesis/development models were employed. It is unclear whether PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment also attenuates CRC metastasis, which is a key CRC death-associated factor. Third, the intramuscular injection of PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP may not be the most effective administration route for delivery of PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP to the body. Finally, it is still unclear how PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP suppresses CRC tumourigenesis and why a combined therapy of mouse CTLA-4Nb mRNA-LNP with PDL1Nb mRNA-LNP fails to synergistically inhibit MC-38 sCRC tumour growth.

sec.title: Conclusions
sec.p: Given that the mouse qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP treatment effectively inhibits CAC and sCRC tumourigenesis and stimulates antitumour immunity, we propose that using human qPDL1Nb mRNA-LNP will be a promising alternative immunotherapy approach in treating human CRC.
